items.title: Section: Genuine Merit Opens — Compassion for the Vicious, Natural Dignity, and Genuine Wisdom in the Teaching's Purity, Wonder, and Reality

items.zh: 又諸菩薩略有五種真實功德。何等為五？一者、於其暴惡毀犯淨戒諸有情所，由是因緣起勝悲心；二者、本性成就具足威儀；三者、於佛所說淨妙真實若教若證，得預智者、聰叡者數；
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas have, in brief, five kinds of genuine merit. What are these five? First, generating supreme compassion, precisely because of this very circumstance, towards beings who are vicious and have violated pure precepts. Second, naturally possessing complete, dignified deportment through one's own inborn nature. Third, being counted among the wise and the clever through what the Buddha taught as pure, wondrous, and true, whether in doctrine or in realisation.
Commentary: Regarding "what the Buddha taught as pure, wondrous, and true" — the Stage Attained Through Hearing explains: what is purity? It is the three natures of purity — the purity of essential nature, the purity of the objective sphere, and the purity of successive stages. What is wonder? It is that the three jewels, Buddha, teaching, and community, are called supremely subtle, since they fall within the very highest of all designations. What is reality? It is suchness and the four noble truths. This should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: Genuine Merit Closes — Faultless Giving, and Refuting Counterfeit Teaching

items.zh: 四者、修行無罪施等善行；五者、開示正法，遮滅一切像似正法。
items.en: Fourth, practising giving and similar wholesome conduct entirely without fault. Fifth, expounding the true teaching so as to refute and extinguish every counterfeit version of the true teaching.

items.title: Section: Undistorted Taming of Beings Opens — Leaving Behind Wrongdoing, and Leaving Behind Desire

items.zh: 又諸菩薩略於十處，無倒調伏所化有情。何等十處？一者、遠離惡行處；二者、遠離諸欲處；
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas, in brief, undistortedly tame the beings being taught in ten places. What are these ten places? First, the place of leaving behind wrongdoing. Second, the place of leaving behind desire.
Commentary: Regarding "the place of leaving behind wrongdoing" and the like — establishing beings in freedom from the unwholesome courses of action is called the place of leaving behind wrongdoing. Establishing beings in freedom from the practice of non-celibate conduct, and from song, dance, and entertainment, is called the place of leaving behind desire.

items.title: Section: Undistorted Taming Continues — Precepts, Guarding the Senses, Right Knowledge, Solitude, and the Two Obstacles to the Path

items.zh: 三者、專精無犯，犯已能出處；四者、密護一切諸根門處；五者、正知住處；六者、離憒鬧處；七者、於遠離處，遠離一切惡尋思處；八者、遠離障處；
items.en:
Third, the place of single-minded, unblemished precept-keeping, and, once a fault has occurred, the place of being able to emerge from it through confession. Fourth, the place of closely guarding every sense-door. Fifth, the place of abiding with right knowledge. Sixth, the place of leaving behind noisy, distracting settings. Seventh, within solitude, the place of leaving behind every unwholesome deliberation. Eighth, the place of leaving behind obstacles.
Commentary: Regarding "the place of leaving behind obstacles" — obstacles are of two kinds, those depending on internal conditions and those depending on external conditions; their characteristics are explained at length in the Stage of Disciples. Establishing beings free of obstacles is called the place of leaving behind obstacles.

items.title: Section: Undistorted Taming Closes — Leaving Behind the Active Afflictions and Their Dormant Seeds, Closing the Second Summary Verse in Full

items.zh: 九者、遠離一切煩惱纏處；十者、遠離一切諸煩惱品諸麁重處。
items.en: Ninth, the place of leaving behind every active manifestation of affliction. Tenth, the place of leaving behind every coarse, dormant seed belonging to the class of afflictions.

items.zh: 復次，嗢拕南曰：諸菩薩受記、墮於決定中、定作、常應作、最勝最為後。

items.title: Section: The Third Summary Verse Opens — Six Marks of Receiving the Buddha's Prophecy of Awakening

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩略由六相，蒙諸如來於其無上正等菩提授與記別。何等為六？一者、安住種性未發心位；二者、已發心位；三者、現在前位；四者、不現前位；五者、有定時限，謂爾所時當證無上正等菩提；六者、無定時限，謂不宣說決定時限，而與授記。
items.en:
This means that bodhisattvas, in brief, through six marks, receive from the tathagatas a prophecy concerning their unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening. What are these six? First, the state of abiding in the lineage without yet having aroused the aspiration for awakening. Second, the state of having already aroused that aspiration. Third, the state of the Buddha appearing in person. Fourth, the state of the Buddha not appearing in person. Fifth, having a fixed time limit, meaning that after such-and-such a time one will attain unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening. Sixth, having no fixed time limit, meaning that the prophecy is given without specifying any definite time.
Commentary: Regarding "the state of the Buddha appearing in person" and the like — receiving a prophecy from the tathagatas who appear directly, face to face, before the bodhisattva is called the state of appearing in person. Its opposite is called the state of not appearing in person.

items.title: Section: Falling Into Certainty Opens — Three Kinds, Beginning With Certainty by Abiding in the Lineage

items.zh: 又諸菩薩略有三種墮於決定。何等為三？一者、安住種性墮於決定；二者、發菩提心墮於決定；三者、不虛修行墮於決定。安住種性墮決定者，謂諸菩薩住種性位，便名為墮決定菩薩。何以故？由此菩薩若遇勝緣，必定堪任證於無上正等覺故。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas, in brief, have three kinds of falling into certainty. What are these three? First, certainty by abiding in the lineage. Second, certainty by arousing the aspiration for awakening. Third, certainty by practice that is never in vain.
Regarding certainty by abiding in the lineage — this means that bodhisattvas who abide in the state of the lineage are thereby called bodhisattvas who have fallen into certainty. Why is this? Because such a bodhisattva, upon encountering excellent conditions, is certainly capable of realising unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening.

items.title: Section: Certainty by Arousing the Aspiration for Awakening — Genuine Realisation of Suchness, Never to Regress

items.zh: 發菩提心墮決定者，謂有一類諸菩薩眾，已於無上正等菩提起決定心，此後乃至證於無上正等菩提，無復退轉。
items.en:
Regarding certainty by arousing the aspiration for awakening — this means that there is a class of bodhisattvas who have already given rise to a decisive resolve towards unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening, and who, from this point onward until they actually realise unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening, never again regress.
Commentary: Regarding "certainty by arousing the aspiration for awakening" and the like — the arousal of the aspiration for awakening spoken of here means the arousal that comes with realising the true nature of phenomena, not an arousal grounded in conventional, worldly terms. The Compendium of Establishments explains: one who arouses the aspiration through realising the true nature of phenomena is someone who, having already passed through the first incalculable eon, has already realised the bodhisattva's ground of utmost joy, has already entered the bodhisattva's fixed stage free of arising, has already truly known unsurpassed awakening and the means to it, has already understood that one's own person draws near, and equally near, to the great fruit of awakening — realising that self and other are entirely equal, thereby gaining a great sense of self — and has already arrived at not dwelling in either the flow of birth-and-death or the extinction of nirvana with regard to the bodhisattva path, thereby gaining a vast, expansive intention. Because of this, such a one never regresses from the great aspiration for awakening — this is called the arousal that comes with realising the true nature of phenomena. This meaning corresponds exactly.

items.title: Section: Certainty by Practice Never in Vain — Ten Kinds of Mastery Attained From the Eighth Ground Onward

items.zh: 不虛修行墮決定者，謂諸菩薩已得自在，普於一切利有情行，如其所欲，隨所造修終無空過。
items.en: Regarding certainty by practice that is never in vain — this means that bodhisattvas who have already attained mastery, in universally benefiting sentient beings through their conduct, accomplish exactly what they intend, and whatever they undertake and cultivate is never carried out in vain.

items.title: Section: The Eighth and Ninth Grounds Named by Their Ten Masteries — Closing All Three Kinds of Certainty in Full

items.zh: 於此三種墮決定中，依於最後墮決定位，諸佛如來授諸菩薩墮決定記。
items.en:
Commentary: Regarding "certainty by practice that is never in vain" and the like — this refers to the ground of certainty and the ground of certain conduct, both called falling into certainty. Because the bodhisattva of the ground of certainty, roused and guided by the Buddha's own awakening, gives rise to boundless emanation-bodies of wondrous wisdom and attains the ten kinds of mastery, this passage speaks of having already attained mastery. And because the bodhisattva of the ground of certain conduct holds thoroughly pure intention towards the benefit and ease of every sentient being, this passage speaks of universally benefiting beings.
Among these three kinds of falling into certainty, it is in dependence on the final position of falling into certainty that the tathagata buddhas bestow upon bodhisattvas the prophecy of having fallen into certainty.

items.title: Section: Five Things a Bodhisattva Definitely Must Do Opens — Arousing the Aspiration for Awakening, and Deep Compassion for Beings

items.zh: 又諸菩薩略有五處定所應作。若不作已，終不堪任證於無上正等菩提。何等為五？一者、發菩提心；二者、於諸有情深生哀愍；
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas, in brief, have five places where they definitely must act. If these are not done, one will never be capable of realising unsurpassed, correct, complete awakening. What are these five? First, arousing the aspiration for awakening.
Commentary: Regarding "arousing the aspiration for awakening" — this refers to a bodhisattva's very first arousal of that aspiration. Through this arousal, one gains the sustaining support for all bodhisattva applied effort. This should be understood as explained in the chapter on the lineage.
Second, generating deep, sorrowful compassion for sentient beings.
Commentary: Regarding "generating deep, sorrowful compassion for sentient beings" — this refers to a bodhisattva's cultivation of great compassion. For the tathagatas teach that a bodhisattva's awakening is established upon compassion itself.

items.title: Section: Blazing Diligence, Skilful Cultivation of the Five Sciences, and Never Growing Weary — Closing All Five Requirements

items.zh: 三者、熾然精進，四者、於諸明處方便修習，五者、無有厭倦。
items.en: Third, blazing diligence. Fourth, skilfully cultivating the sciences. Fifth, never growing weary.

items.title: Section: Five Things a Bodhisattva Should Always Be Doing Opens — Freedom From Heedlessness, and Refuge for the Destitute

items.zh: 又諸菩薩於其五處常所應作。何等為五？一者、於不放逸常所應作；二者、無依無怙、有苦有貧諸有情所，常應為作依怙等事；
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas, in five places, should always be acting. What are these five? First, always acting to remain free of heedlessness. Second, always acting as refuge and support for beings who have no refuge or protector, and who suffer and are destitute.

items.title: Section: Constant Offering to the Buddhas, and Constantly Examining Oneself for Fault Through Six Aspects of Mind

items.zh: 三者、於諸如來常應供養；四者、常應遍知有失、無失；
items.en:
Third, always making offerings to the tathagatas. Fourth, always thoroughly knowing whether there is fault or no fault.
Commentary: Regarding "always thoroughly knowing whether there is fault or no fault" — this means that bodhisattvas, while diligently cultivating the precept of gathering wholesome teachings, should, in brief, skilfully examine six aspects of mind; and within the precept of benefiting sentient beings, should correctly examine six areas of conduct. Their characteristics are explained at length in the Decisions section. Fault and freedom from fault should be understood as explained there.

items.title: Section: The Great Aspiration for Awakening as Constant Guide — Closing All Five Things Always to Be Done

items.zh: 五者、一切所作若行、若住諸作意中，大菩提心恒為導首。如是五種，是諸菩薩常所應作。
items.en:
Fifth, in every mental application accompanying whatever one does, whether moving or staying still, the great aspiration for awakening is always the guide that leads the way.
These five, then, are what bodhisattvas should always be doing.

items.title: Section: Ten Supreme States Opens — Bodhisattva Lineage, the First Arousal of Bodhicitta, Diligence and Wisdom, and Loving Speech

items.zh: 又諸菩薩有十種法，一切菩薩許為最勝，特為第一，建立在於最上法中。何等為十？一者、菩薩種性，諸種性中最為殊勝；二者、最初發心，於諸正願最為殊勝；三者、精進、般若，普於一切波羅蜜多最為殊勝；四者、愛語攝事，於諸攝事最為殊勝；
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas have ten teachings that all bodhisattvas acknowledge as supreme, specifically foremost, established among the very highest teachings. What are these ten? First, the bodhisattva lineage is the most excellent among all lineages. Second, the very first arousal of the aspiration for awakening is the most excellent among all correct vows. Third, diligence and wisdom are, among all the perfections, the most excellent. Fourth, loving speech, among the means of gathering beings, is the most excellent.

items.title: Section: The Tathagata Supreme Among All Beings, Compassion Supreme Among the Immeasurables, and the Fourth Dhyana Supreme Among Meditative Absorptions

items.zh: 五者、如來世尊，於諸有情最為殊勝；六者、悲愍有情，於諸無量最為殊勝；七者、第四靜慮，於諸靜慮最為殊勝；
items.en: Fifth, the tathagata, the world-honoured one, is the most excellent among all sentient beings. Sixth, compassion for beings, among the immeasurables, is the most excellent. Seventh, the fourth dhyana, among the meditative absorptions, is the most excellent.

items.title: Section: Emptiness Supreme Among the Three Concentrations, Cessation Supreme Among Absorptions, and Pure Skilful Means Supreme of All — Closing the Third Summary Verse in Full

items.zh: 八者、空三摩地，於三等持最為殊勝；九者、滅盡等至，於諸等至最為殊勝；十者、如前所說所有清淨方便善巧，普於一切方便善巧最為殊勝。
items.en: Eighth, the concentration on emptiness, among the three forms of concentrated absorption, is the most excellent. Ninth, the absorption of cessation, among all meditative attainments, is the most excellent. Tenth, the pure skilful means already explained above are, among the entirety of skilful means, the most excellent.

blocks.text: The second and third summary verses of the qualities chapter. Genuine merit mirrors yesterday's counterfeit merit. Then prophecy, certainty, what a bodhisattva must always do, and ten things that are "supreme".

"Second, naturally possessing complete, dignified deportment," the opposite of feigning it. Master Cháng Bǎi: not a fake purity. Venerable Miào Jìng: "feigning" refers to the inner deceit, not the outward look.

Venerable Miào Jìng: 密 means tight, with not a single gap. Master Cháng Bǎi: when the six faculties meet their objects, know it is only the mind's false discrimination; do not grasp signs or details. (Ru-Yi's "secretly" misses this sense.)
A summary verse: the bodhisattva's prophecy, falling into certainty, what must be done, what should always be done, and the supreme states, which today's remaining sections explain in order.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha also declares when the bodhisattva will awaken, the name of the land, and who the retinue will be. Venerable Miào Jìng: you can see this in the *Lotus Sūtra*.
Venerable Miào Jìng: this is arousal through realising the dharma-nature, ultimate bodhicitta; afflictions cannot overcome their precepts, concentration, and wisdom.
Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary people's vows are usually empty; but like Avalokiteśvara, the bodhisattva appears in a thousand places when called from a thousand places.
Master Cháng Bǎi: only when great compassion and prajñā are both fully mature can one become a buddha; prajñā without great compassion cannot.
Venerable Miào Jìng: those who suffer and cannot escape are "without support"; the poor who struggle to live are "without protector". The usual reading, "without parents", is too narrow.

"Diligence and wisdom are supreme among all perfections; loving speech is supreme among the means of gathering." Master Cháng Bǎi: without prajñā leading, the other perfections become mere worldly merit.

Venerable Miào Jìng: the second absorption has joy, the third pleasure, and these disturb the mind; the fourth best supports calm and insight. Master Cháng Bǎi: resting in the fourth absorption, the Buddha contemplated the twelve links and attained awakening.
Both lecturers: once emptiness is accomplished, wishlessness and signlessness come easily. Venerable Miào Jìng: the attainment of cessation is "a nirvāṇa-like state placed in the body".
Genuine and counterfeit merit can look the same from outside. Venerable Miào Jìng's point is that the difference is inside: deceit, or its absence.

quiz.q: What is the second genuine merit, and which counterfeit does it oppose?
options: naturally dignified deportment; opposite of feigned deportment
quiz.why: "Second, naturally possessing complete, dignified deportment" — the opposite of "feigning dignified deportment." Master Cháng Bǎi: not a fake purity. Venerable Miào Jìng: "feigning" refers to the inner deceit, not the outward look.

quiz.q: The fourth place — "密護 every sense-door" — is rendered "secretly guarding." How do the lectures read 密?
options: Miào Jìng: tightly, without a single gap; Cháng Bǎi: when faculties meet objects, knowing it's only false discrimination — not grasping signs or details
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 密 means tight — not a single gap. Master Cháng Bǎi: when the six faculties meet their objects, know it's only the mind's false discrimination — don't grasp signs or details. "Secretly" misses the sense.

quiz.q: For the fifth mark of prophecy — "with a fixed time" — what does Master Cháng Bǎi say the Buddha declares?
options: when they will awaken, the name of their land, who their retinue will be
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha also declares when the bodhisattva will awaken, the name of the land, who the retinue will be. Venerable Miào Jìng: you can see this if you read the Lotus Sūtra.

quiz.q: What kind of arousal is meant in "certainty by arousing the aspiration"?
options: arousal through realising the dharma-nature, ultimate bodhicitta — Miào Jìng: afflictions cannot overcome their precepts, concentration, wisdom; Cháng Bǎi: not one that stays at conventional naming
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: this is arousal through realising the dharma-nature — ultimate bodhicitta; afflictions cannot overcome their precepts, concentration, and wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: not an arousal that stays at conventional labels — it transcends names.

quiz.q: "Practice never in vain — accomplishing what they intend." How does Master Cháng Bǎi contrast ordinary people?
options: ordinary people's vows rarely come true — empty wishes; bodhisattvas, like Avalokiteśvara, appear wherever called
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary people's vows are hard to fulfil — usually empty; like Avalokiteśvara, appearing in a thousand places when called from a thousand places. Venerable Miào Jìng: "as they wish" refers to vows.

quiz.q: On the second — "deep compassion for beings" — what does Master Cháng Bǎi stress?
options: both great compassion and prajñā must fully mature; prajñā without compassion cannot yield buddhahood
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: only when great compassion and prajñā are both fully mature can one become a buddha; prajñā without great compassion cannot. Venerable Miào Jìng: the bodhisattva's future awakening is built by great compassion.

quiz.q: The second constant duty is being refuge for "those without support or protector, suffering and poor." How do the lectures explain it?
options: Miào Jìng: suffering without escape is "no support," poverty "no protector" — "no parents" is too narrow; Cháng Bǎi: constantly relieving and protecting, freeing the suffering from distress
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: those who suffer and cannot escape are "without support"; the poor who struggle to live are "without protector" — the usual reading, "without parents," is too narrow. Master Cháng Bǎi: constantly offering relief, protection, and support so the suffering escape distress.

quiz.q: Among the perfections and among the means of gathering, which are supreme?
quiz.why: "Diligence and wisdom are supreme among all perfections; loving speech is supreme among the means of gathering." Master Cháng Bǎi: diligence is the driving force, prajñā the wisdom; without prajñā leading, the other perfections become mere worldly merit.

quiz.q: "The fourth dhyāna is supreme." The English note says it's because it escapes the three calamities. What reasons do the lectures give?
options: Miào Jìng: joy and pleasure in lower absorptions disturb the mind; the fourth best supports calm and insight; Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha awakened in it contemplating dependent origination — concentration and wisdom balanced
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the second absorption has joy, the third pleasure, and these disturb the mind; the fourth is supreme and best supports calm and insight. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha, resting in the fourth absorption, contemplated the twelve links and attained awakening. The calamities reason is not the lecturers'.

quiz.q: Why is the absorption of cessation supreme, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: it is definitely untainted, most peaceful — "a nirvāṇa-like state placed in the body"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: cessation is definitely untainted — especially excellent and most peaceful, "a nirvāṇa-like state placed in the body." Master Cháng Bǎi: offerings to a noble one just emerged from cessation bring results in this very life.
